verdict: Caution on Hyderabad residential developers: lend only to RERA-clean, collections-led builders with escrow discipline; avoid any sponsor with double-sale or allotment-cancellation disputes.
title: Hyderabad residential real estate: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What the business physically is
A Hyderabad residential developer buys land, converts it into flats over 3-4 years, and gets paid mostly by homebuyers in instalments tied to construction milestones, not on handover. **Cash sits in the buyer's instalment schedule and the escrow, not in the P&L.** So when a proposal lands, check the RERA-registered project's collection schedule against the construction timeline; if collections run ahead of construction, ask where the surplus is parked. Cost is land plus construction; the minister says GST 2.0 and the new tax regime cut construction costs by an estimated 3-5% [1], but that benefit only reaches the developer's margin if pricing holds. Pricing power is local: it depends on micro-market absorption, not on the builder's brand alone.

## What has changed now
Two things. First, policy pressure to pass GST savings to homebuyers [1] means **do not underwrite margin expansion from the 3-5% cost cut**; treat it as a buffer, not profit. Second, and more important for credit, TGRERA is actively restraining developers: nine flats in Tellapur frozen over double-sale allegations [2], and Pacifica restrained from cancelling a Bachupally allotment after a delayed-possession and additional-payment dispute [3]. **These are conduct failures, and they precede cash-flow failures.** So when a proposal lands, pull the promoter's TGRERA order history; if any restraint or double-sale order exists, ask for the escrow reconciliation and the buyer-refund liability before sanctioning.

## Where the growth is
Peer results show the demand is real: Brigade's Q2 profit rose 29% to Rs 219 crore on sales of Rs 1,827 crore, with 2.4 million sq ft launched [4], and it plans over 7 million sq ft of launches in H2 FY27 [6]. Aditya Birla Real Estate's collections rose 31% year-over-year to Rs 713 crore [7]. **Pursue Hyderabad builders with a live RERA pipeline, clean order history and collections tracking construction.** Avoid sponsors whose model depends on buyer cancellation or re-pricing sold flats [3]. Note the sources say little about Hyderabad-specific volumes; lean on first principles and these peers.

## How to grow safely
Structure against the escrow, not the balance sheet. **Take monthly: escrow bank statement, RERA quarterly progress report, collection-vs-construction certificate, and unsold inventory by tower.** Covenant that withdrawal from escrow needs our sign-off, and that any TGRERA order is notified within 7 days. Peer discipline is instructive: Brigade's debt-to-equity was 0.31 with 85% of debt backed by rental cash flow [5]; ask every borrower for the same split between sold-and-collected and rental-backed debt.

## Early-warning signs
- Monthly escrow inflows falling below construction spend for two months -> freeze further disbursement and inspect the site.
- Any TGRERA complaint or restraint order (event-based) -> re-underwrite the project and demand buyer-refund provisioning.
- Rising unsold inventory in one tower (monthly) -> cut exposure and re-price the sanction.
- Collections running ahead of construction (quarterly) -> ask where the surplus sits and ring-fence it.
watch: Inflows below construction spend for 2 months -> freeze disbursement, site inspection

Rental-backed share falling below peer norm -> require higher equity contribution
